title: AA-P10-LIVE development smoke LS-04 (or_claim_supported_alternative); source text from study-forensics-021
prompt: The virtual tutoring program improved struggling students' reading progress or reduced their school absenteeism.
context: A randomized controlled trial tested a virtual reading tutoring program in a rural school district. The program paired live online tutors with small groups of struggling elementary students for ten-week sessions. Students who completed around forty tutoring sessions gained roughly two additional months of reading progress compared with peers in the control condition. Even those attending fewer sessions showed modest gains. Researchers emphasised that consistent participation was critical and highlighted that the program delivered results at a lower cost than typical high-dose tutoring.
